title: Sanctions, Fraud, Bribery and Tax Evasion
summary: The board's oversight of the financial crime risks beyond money laundering, where liability is often strict and failures can be sudden and severe.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The board's oversight of the financial crime risks beyond money laundering, where liability is often strict and failures can be sudden and severe.
Learning Objectives: Explain the board's obligations under sanctions, anti-bribery and tax evasion regimes
Evaluate whether the firm has adequate procedures to prevent these offences
Assess the firm's fraud exposure, including payment scams and internal fraud
Syllabus: Sanctions screening, ownership and control, and evasion typologies
Fraud risk: customers, staff, third parties and emerging scams
Bribery and corruption: gifts, intermediaries and adequate procedures
Failure to prevent the facilitation of tax evasion
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members, especially on risk and audit committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for financial crime, compliance and operations
Company secretaries and heads of governance supporting board oversight
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No specialist background in financial crime compliance is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
